thread_b.role: busy-poll / datagram reader checking queue tail locklessly

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([READ sk_receive_queue.prev @281]) from thread_b (single-access read of a queue link that assumes no concurrent conflicting write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@__sock_queue_rcv_skb:477 = __skb_queue_tail(list, skb) updates the queue .prev/.next links concurrently in the producer context
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the producer updates the queue under sk->sk_receive_queue.lock; the busy-poll reader reads the queue links WITHOUT taking that lock (busy poll is lockless by design), so no common lock serializes the read against the producer write
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho = atomic(single access) on queue-link pointers broken by a concurrent unsynchronized list update -> KCSAN data race (torn/stale link read)

fix_maps_to: patch replaces skb_queue_empty() with skb_queue_empty_lockless() in the busy-poll readers (chtls/nvme-tcp/tcp/sctp) and wraps __skb_try_recv_datagram's tail check in READ_ONCE(sk->sk_receive_queue.prev). Marked-access only -- it declares the lockless read intentional; it adds NO serialize/order/counts guarantee, so it does not 'establish' rho.
recall_risk_notes: Same *_ONCE/lockless family as the other KCSAN net-stack races: a benign single-field torn-read race silenced by skb_queue_empty_lockless()/READ_ONCE (commit: 'Busy polling usually runs without locks'). The read is intentionally lockless, so there is no SC ordering invariant -- the design's anti-pure-syntactic-race stance (4.6.3) means it likely won't raise it or will treat it as benign. Additional risks: (1) the racing read is one of many sibling busy-poll sites spread across 6 files (chtls_io, nvme/host/tcp, datagram, sock, tcp, sctp/socket) all touching the same sk_receive_queue, so object identity must unify across files; (2) cross-context MHP (softirq producer vs task busy-poll reader) must be modeled, and the producer DOES hold the receive-queue spinlock, so keep/reject must conclude the busy-poll reader lacks the common lock.
